sources.cite: StatPearls. Tension Pneumothorax (last updated 2025-07-07), StatPearls Publishing
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch with quotes: 'Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis'; in an unstable patient 'immediate needle decompression must be performed without delay', and imaging such as a chest x-ray only 'if the patient is stable'; signs include severe respiratory distress, hypotension, tachycardia, absent breath sounds, jugular venous distension and tracheal deviation; needle at the second anterior intercostal space, midclavicular line, or 'when time permits' the fifth intercostal space, anterior axillary line, with long angiocatheters (>8 cm); iatrogenic causes include subclavian or internal jugular catheterization and barotrauma from positive pressure ventilation.

brief.situation: 09:00 in the medical ICU. You are the RN. Mr. Ortega, 66, on a ventilator for pneumonia, had a right subclavian central line placed by the resident at 08:30; the confirming chest X-ray is ordered but not done. The ventilator is alarming for high peak pressure, and his saturation is dropping.
handover: Volume control, FiO2 40%, PEEP 5. Peak pressures were 26-28 cmH2O all night. Sedated, comfortable at 08:00.
Arterial line in place. Norepinephrine is not running.
The ICU provider is on the unit; a portable chest X-ray takes about 15 minutes to arrive.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
He is changing minute by minute. The provider takes a couple of minutes to reach the bed.
Partway through you are asked to write what you think is happening. A debrief scores what you did.

source.note: Untreated, the tension reaches arrest in about 11 minutes. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.
Obstructive shock with pulseless electrical activity. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.
Needle decompression releases most of the tension at once. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

More positive pressure worsens a tension pneumothorax (StatPearls lists positive-pressure barotrauma as a cause). FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.
The ICU provider reaches the bed about 2 min after a stat call.
Fetching the kit when nobody brought it: about 90 s.
A portable chest X-ray arrives about 15 min after the call.
Authored target: the chest examined within 3 min of the alarm. FLAG.
Authored target: immediate decompression asked for within 5 min. FLAG.
The case ends 5 min after decompression.

assess.label: Examine the chest: breath sounds both sides, chest movement, trachea, neck veins

then.log: Breath sounds returning on the right; trachea midline.
No breath sounds on the right, the right chest barely moves and is hyperresonant; trachea shifted to the left; neck veins distended; dusky lips. BP {sbp}/{dbp}.

suction.label: Suction the endotracheal tube (is it blocked?)

effects.log: The catheter passes easily; scant secretions. The tube is not blocked.

bag.label: Take him off the ventilator and bag by hand with 100% oxygen

effects.log: The bag is very stiff to squeeze. SpO2 {spo2}%.

fio2.label: Turn FiO2 to 100% on the ventilator

peep.label: Raise PEEP to 10 to improve oxygenation

effects.log: Peak pressure climbs and the blood pressure drops further.

kit.label: Bring the decompression kit (long 14-gauge catheter) and the chest tube tray to the bed

effects.log: Decompression kit and chest tube tray open at the bedside.

fluid.label: 500 mL crystalloid bolus while help comes

effects.log: Bolus running. It may buy a little pressure; it does not relieve the tension.

Needle decompression on the right with the kit you set up: a rush of air. SpO2 and BP climb. A chest tube follows.
Provider: 'Where's the decompression kit?' Someone runs for it.

why.question: What is happening to Mr. Ortega, and what must happen before anything else?

parts.label: Recognition
parts.criteria: Names a right tension pneumothorax after a subclavian line on positive-pressure ventilation: rising peak pressure, falling SpO2 and BP, absent right breath sounds, tracheal shift, distended neck veins; rules out a blocked tube.
parts.modelAnswer: A right tension pneumothorax from the subclavian line, made worse by the ventilator: high peaks, falling sats and pressure, no breath sounds on the right, trachea pushed left, neck veins up. The tube is clear.

parts.label: Priorities
parts.criteria: Treats it as a clinical diagnosis: immediate decompression before any X-ray; bags with 100% oxygen; brings the kit; does not raise PEEP.
parts.modelAnswer: Call the provider for decompression now, not a film. Bag on 100% oxygen, kit and chest tube tray at the bed, no PEEP increase. The X-ray comes after he is decompressed.

expertPath.text: Look at the patient, not the alarm: SpO2 falling, BP falling, peaks high. Examine: no right breath sounds, trachea left, neck veins up.
Off the ventilator, bag on 100%: very stiff. Suction: tube clear.
Stat call: tension pneumothorax, decompress now. Kit and chest tube tray to the bed. No PEEP increase.
Needle decompression on arrival; chest tube; X-ray afterwards.

arrest.headline: Cardiac arrest
arrest.body: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis. An unstable patient is decompressed before any film; waiting for imaging or adding positive pressure leads to arrest.

decompressedFast.headline: Decompressed before imaging
decompressedFast.body: You treated the patient rather than the alarm, found the signs, gave 100% oxygen, asked for decompression now and had the kit ready. That is the expert path.

decompressedLate.headline: Decompressed, by a slower route
decompressedLate.body: Check how soon you examined the chest, raised the oxygen, and asked for decompression rather than a film.

time_up.headline: Never decompressed
time_up.body: Unstable plus absent breath sounds and tracheal shift: decompress first.

scoring.modelReasoning: A high-pressure alarm with falling SpO2 and blood pressure half an hour after a subclavian line, in a patient on positive pressure, is a tension pneumothorax until proven otherwise: absent breath sounds on one side, tracheal shift away, distended neck veins and obstructive shock. It is a clinical diagnosis; in an unstable patient needle decompression comes at once and imaging waits until he is stable. Bag with 100% oxygen (a stiff bag confirms the problem) and suction to rule out a blocked tube; do not raise PEEP. Have a long catheter and the chest tube tray at the bed so the provider decompresses on arrival.

chapters.label: The provider is on the way

siteQ.ask: While the provider comes: where does StatPearls place the needle when time permits?

choices.label: Fifth intercostal space, anterior axillary line

siteQ.explain: The second intercostal space in the midclavicular line, or when time permits the fifth intercostal space in the anterior axillary line, with a long catheter (over 8 cm).
